title: Canapaukah / Dutch Kills
summary: Canapaukah is associated with Dutch Kills, the north branch of Newtown Creek in Long Island City. The early record identifies the waterway generally rather than a precise point.
why_this_matters: Canapaukah preserves a Native name for the Dutch Kills branch of Newtown Creek, interpreted as a fenced or enclosed water-place. That meaning invites attention to water control, creek edges, and local observation in a landscape now heavily urbanized and industrial. Western Long Island and Queens remain part of Native geography, where older waterway names matter even when the shoreline has been dramatically changed.
history_content: The history belongs to the western Long Island creek and mill-dam landscape around Newtown Creek. Dated source details are handled in the timeline.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Canapaukah and Dutch Kills. The name is interpreted as referring to a fenced water-place or enclosed water-place, with the interpretation kept tentative because spellings and boundary language vary across the sources.

Why Place Names Matter

“The place names reveal the influence of the many people who have called this land home.”

— Joanna Dawson, Place Names of Newfoundland and Labrador (2023), review, opening description

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
